grapple.name: Grapple
grapple.summary: Attempt to grab and restrain a creature using an Unarmed Strike.

mechanics.target_restriction: Target must be no more than one size larger than you
mechanics.escape: Target can use Action to escape (Athletics or Acrobatics vs your save DC)

grapple.full_text: When you use the Grapple option of an Unarmed Strike, the target must be no more than one size larger than you. The target must succeed on a saving throw (DC = 8 + your Strength modifier + your proficiency bonus) or gain the Grappled condition. While Grappled, the target's speed is 0 and they cannot benefit from bonuses to speed.

shove.name: Shove
shove.summary: Push a creature away or knock it prone using an Unarmed Strike.

mechanics.target_restriction: Target must be no more than one size larger than you
mechanics.effect: Target is pushed 5 feet or knocked Prone
mechanics.choice: You choose whether to push or knock prone

shove.full_text: When you use the Shove option of an Unarmed Strike, the target must be no more than one size larger than you. The target must succeed on a saving throw (DC = 8 + your Strength modifier + your proficiency bonus) or be pushed up to 5 feet away from you or knocked Prone (your choice).

advantage.name: Advantage
advantage.summary: Roll 2d20 and use the higher result.

mechanics.stacking: Multiple instances of Advantage don't stack

advantage.full_text: When you have Advantage on a d20 roll, roll two d20s and use the higher of the two rolls. If multiple situations grant Advantage, you still roll only two dice. If you have both Advantage and Disadvantage, you roll only one d20.

disadvantage.name: Disadvantage
disadvantage.summary: Roll 2d20 and use the lower result.

mechanics.stacking: Multiple instances of Disadvantage don't stack

disadvantage.full_text: When you have Disadvantage on a d20 roll, roll two d20s and use the lower of the two rolls. If multiple situations impose Disadvantage, you still roll only two dice. If you have both Advantage and Disadvantage, you roll only one d20.

initiative.name: Initiative
initiative.summary: Determines the order of turns in combat.

mechanics.type: Comparative roll (higher is better, not vs DC)
mechanics.ties: DM decides order, or creatures can roll again

initiative.full_text: Initiative determines the order of turns during combat. When combat starts, every participant rolls initiative by making a Dexterity check. The DM ranks the combatants in order from the one with the highest check total to the one with the lowest. This is the initiative order, which is the order in which they act during each round.

opportunity_attack.name: Opportunity Attack
opportunity_attack.summary: Make a melee attack when a creature you can see leaves your reach.

mechanics.trigger: Creature you can see leaves your reach
mechanics.attack: One melee attack with a weapon or Unarmed Strike

opportunity_attack.full_text: You can make an opportunity attack when a hostile creature that you can see moves out of your reach. To make the opportunity attack, you use your Reaction to make one melee attack with a weapon or an Unarmed Strike against the provoking creature. The attack occurs right before the creature leaves your reach. You can avoid provoking opportunity attacks by taking the Disengage action.

critical_hit.name: Critical Hit
critical_hit.summary: Roll all damage dice twice when you roll a 20 on an attack roll.

mechanics.effect: Roll all damage dice twice and add them together, then add modifiers
mechanics.auto_hit: A natural 20 always hits regardless of AC

critical_hit.full_text: When you score a critical hit, you roll all of the attack's damage dice twice and add them together. Then add any relevant modifiers as normal. A critical hit occurs when you roll a 20 on the d20 for an attack roll. A critical hit automatically hits regardless of the target's AC.

cover.name: Cover
cover.summary: Obstacles provide bonuses to AC and Dexterity saving throws.

mechanics.half_cover: +2 bonus to AC and Dexterity saving throws
mechanics.three_quarters_cover: +5 bonus to AC and Dexterity saving throws
mechanics.total_cover: Can't be targeted directly by attacks or spells

cover.full_text: Obstacles can provide cover during combat, making a target harder to harm. A target has Half Cover if an obstacle blocks at least half of its body (+2 to AC and Dexterity saves). A target has Three-Quarters Cover if about three-quarters of it is covered (+5 to AC and Dexterity saves). A target has Total Cover if it is completely concealed (can't be targeted).

armor_stealth_disadvantage.name: Armor Stealth Disadvantage
armor_stealth_disadvantage.summary: Certain armors impose Disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.
armor_stealth_disadvantage.full_text: If the Armor table shows 'Disadvantage' in the Stealth column for an armor type, the wearer has Disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks. Armors that impose this penalty include: Padded Armor, Scale Mail, Half Plate Armor, Ring Mail, Chain Mail, Splint Armor, and Plate Armor.

advantage_disadvantage_cancel.name: Advantage and Disadvantage Canceling
advantage_disadvantage_cancel.summary: If you have both Advantage and Disadvantage, they cancel out and you roll normally (one d20).

mechanics.rule: Multiple instances don't stack - just cancel out
mechanics.result: Roll only one d20 (no advantage or disadvantage)

advantage_disadvantage_cancel.full_text: If circumstances cause a roll to have both Advantage and Disadvantage, you are considered to have neither of them, and you roll one d20. This is true even if multiple circumstances impose Disadvantage and only one grants Advantage, or vice versa. In such a situation, you have neither Advantage nor Disadvantage.

mounted_combat.name: Mounted Combat
mounted_combat.summary: A willing creature that is at least one size larger than you can serve as a mount.

mechanics.size_requirement: Mount must be at least one size larger than rider
mechanics.independent_mount: Acts on its own initiative, can move and act freely
mechanics.controlled_mount: Acts on your initiative, can only Dash, Disengage, or Dodge

mounted_combat.full_text: A willing creature that is at least one size larger than a rider and that has an appropriate anatomy can serve as a mount. During your move, you can mount a creature that is within 5 feet of you or dismount. Doing so costs an amount of movement equal to half your speed. A mount can be either controlled or independent. A controlled mount can move and act only on your turn and has only three action options: Dash, Disengage, and Dodge. An independent mount acts on its own initiative and can move and act as it chooses.

size_categories.name: Size Categories
size_categories.summary: Creatures are categorized by size: Tiny, Small, Medium, Large, Huge, Gargantuan.
size_categories.full_text: Each creature takes up a different amount of space. The Size Categories table shows how much space a creature of a particular size controls in combat. Size categories: Tiny (2.5 by 2.5 ft.), Small (5 by 5 ft.), Medium (5 by 5 ft.), Large (10 by 10 ft.), Huge (15 by 15 ft.), Gargantuan (20 by 20 ft. or larger). Many rules and features reference size categories. For example, you can grapple or shove a creature that is no more than one size larger than you.

hiding.name: Hiding
hiding.summary: You must be heavily obscured or behind total cover to hide, and you can't hide from creatures that can see you clearly.

mechanics.requirements: Must be heavily obscured or behind total cover from creatures you're hiding from
mechanics.discovery: Creatures can use Search action to try to find you

hiding.full_text: The DM decides when circumstances are appropriate for hiding. When you try to hide, you take the Hide action. You can't hide from a creature that can see you clearly. You must be heavily obscured (by fog, darkness, foliage, or similar) or behind total cover from any creature you want to hide from. If you make noise (such as shouting a warning or knocking over a vase), you give away your position. An invisible creature can't be seen, so it can always try to hide.
